newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: IDB grants $107.65 mln loan to Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: IDB grants $107.65 mln loan to Guatemala.

text.p: The Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) said on Wednesday it had approved a $107.65 million loan for Guatemala for infrastructure projects.
The loan, with a 20-year maturity and a variable interest rate, is the largest of its kind since Guatemala ended 36 years of civil war in late December, signing a peace agreement with leftist rebels.
"We are saying that we have confidence in Guatemala," said Iliana Waleska Pastor, the bank's Guatemala representative.
The loan has an initial repayment grace period of five-and-a-half years.
Guatemala's Economy Minister Juan Mauricio Wurmser told Reuters the loan was another sign that peace was paying dividends in the impoverished Central American nation.
He said Guatemala's exports are up and inflation is down, creating an increasingly healthy climate for economic development.

Exports totalled $1.6 billion for the first six months of the year, a 43 percent increase compared to the same period last year and due mainly to "excellent coffee prices" and a growing market in Central America, Wurmser said.
Exports of traditional products rose 60 percent, including an 11 percent increase in coffee exports, he said.

Exports of non-traditional products rose 21 percent, including a 103 percent increase in tobacco exports, a 23 percent increase in the export of plants and flowers, a 22 percent rise in fruit exports and an 11 percent increase in chemical product exports.
Exports to Central American nations increased 33 percent.
Year-over-year inflation was 8.7 percent through the third week in June, compared to 10.3 percent at the same time last year, Wurmser said.
Accumulated inflation was 3.4 percent, compared to 5.4 percent last year, according to official statisitcs. The annual inflation rate averaged 11 percent for the past five years.
